utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to make this point when it came to -- when the point came to admit the video, but I'll ask it now. We're asking a lot of questions about identity, and it would be useful if my friend, the Prosecutor, could try and ascertain the time frame of this videotape. If that could perhaps be established with the witness, that would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will ask the witness, Your Honour, but there will be other witnesses to speak to this videotape.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you know when this event or this ceremony was held?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the first time that you were aware of this ceremony was when, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, did you see this tape in proofing two days ago, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Well, yes, that too, yeah. Are you playing games with me? If I were to say you had already shown it to me, yes, I've seen it, but this is the first time I officially see it. I said that my goal was to establish the truth. Yes. I have seen it before, in your office, but this is the first time that I am officially shown it. So, Your Honour, yes, I have seen this video clip before in the Prosecution's premises. Well, I apologise, anyway. There is no reason for me to be brought into an embarrassing situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd also like to, I believe -- Do you know what -- the transcript, at page 47, line 7, said "Kurban Bajram." Is this the correct phrase? Do you know what this means?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: It is a religious holiday, a Muslim religious holiday. Its name is "Kurban Bajram," and it is tradition. I am, of course, myself an atheist, but this is a traditional day when the Muslims dedicate themselves to the Almighty, and with great -- celebrated by the Muslims with utmost attention and devotion. It is the custom, during the Kurban Bajram, for neighbours to -- the Muslims bring to their friends and to their names the so-called "Kurban," which is sheep meat, which really makes a very good dish when you combine it with cabbage. But this is a Muslim religious holiday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now could we watch the third clip, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The present guests and the 7th" -- "following that," sorry, "the commander of the General Staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Rasim Delic, addressed the honourable ranks of the 7th Muslim Chivalrous Mountain Brigade and all present."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask the tape to be stopped, because I would like to go back and bit a ask the witness to look at all the persons in the videotape and to identify all the persons he is able to identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the tape be played.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Following that, the commander addressed the honourable ranks of the 7th Muslim Chivalrous Mountain Brigade and all present."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you identify these persons?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: The man with the glasses, Sulejman Vranj, he was the head of the Personnel Administration. This other person was a commander. I cannot recall his name. For a while, he was the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to know who was standing -- the second person -- well, can you tell us, for the purpose of the record, which person -- the person in the blue is whom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Sartorio. I don't see a blue colour here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you start with the first person who's just disappearing and go back?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's what I'd like to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's what I intended to do, but the person who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: However, don't use colour, but use the position of the person in the row.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. We have to start again from the beginning. It's very fast, but we have to stop it right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Following that..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The same introductory remarks as before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this man who is holding his cap, this is the head of the Administration for Personnel and Mobilisation and Organisational Affairs. His name is Sulejman Vranj. He was at the Main Staff throughout all that time. In the center - but bear with me, I'm not quite sure - in the center, for a while, this person was the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, I believe from its very establishment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can I just, before you establish the time frame, so we can get it on the record, of this video, which is 3.46.1 -- 00:03:46:1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the former commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, the man in the black dress in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just remember this very minute. His name was Brzina. It takes some remembering after 15 years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome. The next one is the commander of the 7th Corps, and he spoke just a while ago, as we saw. That is Alagic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask we start with the first person in the video, and I believe it's backwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The person who's holding the brown notebook or briefcase, that is the first person you named, Sulejman Vranj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I think it's clear now. Is it clear to Your Honours? The witness went backwards, Your Honour. Instead of starting with the right and moving left, he started at the left and moved right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've got a different problem, or at least I do. I see you. I don't see these people that you are talking about. Okay. Fine. Now I'm with you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So now can we -- can we proceed just slowly too. If there are other people on the tape, we'll just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, who is the person with the beret, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Halid Cengic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you identify the person next to him in the vest, or do you need to see it further?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry. Can we go back, Your Honours, just a bit? It's only a second, but it will need to pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are you able to identify anyone else in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: The man in the robe is the reis ullema, Effendi Ceric, the first one to my left or the first one to your right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is a -- what you mentioned, a "reis." I'm looking for it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's "ullema."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what a "reis ullema" is?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: It's the supreme, religious minister in the religious community. Just like General Delic was in the army. The reis ullema is the supreme leader in the community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, if you could control your witness to please go in a particular order. Now, he's been telling these people starting from our right. He jumped to the man in the suit. He's now telling us about the man in the robe. We're not going to know who's who here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The person with the beret, I believe, did you identify him as Cengic; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then the person next to Mr. Cengic, standing there with his hands folded in front of him, in a vest, can you identify this person?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: I said, "No."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then the next, the person next to him, in the suit, are you able to identify this person?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then the person next to him is the reis ullema?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Effendi Ceric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to put this time of this into the record, Your Honours, 00:03:52:7. May we proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if we can go on. I'm not sure we can stop it at that second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sure you can. It goes for a long time before --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It can be stopped. Just go back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed. Do what you can do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "First of all, I'm duty-bound to convey to you in this place the greetings from the president of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and your honorary commander, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, who was not able to come here from Sarajevo and attend this ceremony, but he is always with you, and you can count him as a participant in these ceremony's proceedings. "I'm also greatly honoured, during these festive days, to be able to congratulate the 7th Muslim Brigade for the honour of bearing the name 'Chivalrous.' Our circumstances have arisen so that we may, during these days of the Bajram, when all the Muslims in the world are celebrating the most important holiday, give one of our most elite units this name, which it has deserved by virtue of its combat action so far in the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Bosniak Muslims. "The title 'Chivalrous' is only a stimulus for the future engagement of both this unit and other units on the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Up until yesterday, we asked you to participate in the defence of the Bosnian Muslim people and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and thank God that this task has been accomplished. "Now we have other tasks to accomplish. You, who as of today are knights, a chivalrous brigade, must be the honour and pride of our liberation struggle, for we have embarked on the liberation of our occupied territories, and only our strength and our motivation and our commitment can bring us what we seek. As the experience of the past three years has shown us, we cannot expect help from anyone else in any way in this just struggle. "All that remains is a conviction in our own strength, in our own unity, in our own engagement, and that has shown itself up until now as the only right path. Therefore, let the honour that has been rightfully bestowed on you today serve as a stimulus for your further combat, your further engagement in the liberation of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "I am confident that you will be at the forefront in carrying out your tasks, as you have been up until now, and that you will carry the banner of freedom throughout the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the name of that, in the name of that, I wish you every success in combat, and many battle the results for the benefit of the Bosnian Muslim people."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That was the end of the clip that we intended to show, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The only problem is that we didn't get to know who the other people are that were supposed to be identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if we could go back just a few seconds. There we go. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Starting with the person on the right, as you're looking at the screen, I believe you identified him in the previous clip. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: If this is the young man with a band, what I said was I could not identify him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you to start looking -- as you look at the screen, you look at the person on your extreme right, the person in the robe would be white --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: The reis ullema, Effendi Mustafa Ceric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you identify the person standing next to him, on his right, but it is the next person over?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: No. I cannot recognise -- I do not recognise that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the third person is?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Next to him is Mahmuljin, Sakib Mahmuljin, the commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you describe, is Sakib Mahmuljin the person in the middle of these five persons?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Yes. He is in the center.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And is he wearing a belt around his waist or some sort of -- it looks like a belt?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: It is a military soldier's belt.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, could you identify the person to his right, who is dressed in camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: That is Rasim Delic, the commander of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you already testified that you cannot identify the person next to him with the headband; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like, for the record, to put in the time of this particular picture. It's 00:07:47:9. May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We are finished with this video. Yes, I would ask it be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the three clips that we just saw will be Exhibit number 349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with the term "Mujahedin"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in your capacity as deputy commander of the army, when is the first term -- first time that you heard of this term in connection with the army?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: The first time was sometime around the 18th of June, 1993, at a morning briefing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who was in attendance at this morning briefing?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: The commander was, and his deputies were, heads of administrations also.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? Commander Delic, I assume that's who you mean, Commander Delic.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: Yes, Commander Delic was there. The head of the Intelligence Administration was there, Hajrulahovic; the head of the Security Administration, Mr. Jasarevic; and the head of the Administration for Moral Guidance, Brigic [Realtime transcript read in error "Brkic"]; and others.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Tell us the content of the conversation with regard to the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: It's not "Brkic." It's different. It is "Brigic," B-R-I-G-I-C.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, what was discussed at this meeting with regard to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: We received information about a group of soldiers from foreign countries, and the details in that connection were provided by the head of the Intelligence Administration, the head of the Security Administration. That was the essence of it. And the others, we, the others, took part in the discussion. The reports spoke about the conduct of a group of alien citizens, conduct that was not befitting that of members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. After a discussion that lasted for about an hour, all the present proposed to Commander Delic that the problem was these people, so we are not talking about any unit. According to the information that we had received, this was no unit. So that we were to discuss this problem with the president of the Presidency, Mr. Izetbegovic, in order for this question of this group of foreign people to be resolved. In the assessment of the head of the Intelligence Administration, the group involved between 300 and 400 people. It was then assessed, it was stated that these were people most of whom had been dispatched by intelligence services, and then they were named, Israel, the French service, the British even, and that most of them could speak the local languages, so to speak, having been educated --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You may as well finish your statement.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: -- having been educated in the space of the former Yugoslavia. It was our position and our proposal that Mr. Delic should propose that, first of all, this group of foreign citizens, of citizens of other states, should be sent back to wherever they had come from and, two, or (b), that they should be organised as a unit and, as such, comprised within the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is that an "and" or an "or." It says in the transcript "should be sent back to where they had come from, and to." It can't be both, so ...

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: What I said was "and under (b), that they should become part of," et cetera, to be established as a unit and be comprised as such within the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is 1314.22 where you have the "(b)."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I see the "(b)," but, sir, you said: "a proposal that Mr. Delic should propose that, first of all, this group of citizens, of citizens of other states, should be sent back to wherever they had come from, and, two," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Two or(b)."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry. I didn't see the "or." Excuse me, Your Honour. That was my fault.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what was General Delic's response to this?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: He simply accepted this proposal. There was no need for any comment on his part. He acknowledged our considerations. I'm quite sure that had he had any different proposal, he would have said so. We were all, of course, together shouldering the responsibility for everything that was transpiring. It was not just Delic's responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, when you mentioned that they were committing -- or they were, at page 59, line 13, "conduct that was not befitting that of members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: According to the information that we'd received that day, they were not participating in operations with members of the army. They were confronting the local police. They were having conflicts with the local police. They were actually making their logistical -- acquiring their logistical supplies by violent ways, because they were not part of the army which actually took care of logistical support in the regular way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I just have a few more questions in this area, Your Honour, and then could we finish? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Had you heard any information about any connection between these persons and civilians?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: I don't know what connections between those people and civilians you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any reports that they, these people, the people that you were speaking of at this meeting, were conducting unbefitting conduct with regard to civilians? You just mentioned police officers, but I'm asking you if you also received information with regard to civilians.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: What I meant was that they actually acquired their supplies, their food, by violent ways. They simply took it from the shops or they just simply wrestled it away from individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you know what was done as a result of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss or hear another discussion about the Mujahedin in any other meetings after this meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN DIVJAK
utterances.text: I did not attend any such meetings, if any were held.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We may stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I may have misunderstood your testimony just a while ago, but I thought you said that the proposal was made either to decide to send all these foreigners back to where they came from or, in the alternative, to try and integrate them properly into the army so that they would behave according to the rules; and then you said that General Delic accepted the proposal, and I was just unsure about which of the two proposals was it that he accepted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only learned from the press that, I don't know under whose suggestion, Mr. Delic wrote an order that a unit should be formed and made part of the 3rd Corps. Therefore, until recently, I never knew that Commander Delic issued such an order. Whether it was his decision or whether it was given to him as a task by the supreme commander, well, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. But you were there present at the meeting on 18th of June, 1993, at the morning meeting with Delic and with the head of the Intelligence Service and the heads of the other services that you mentioned. And you told us that the head of the Intelligence Service informed the group, at the meeting -- at the morning meeting on 18th June, about these foreigners and told the members present at that meeting about all the misconduct that the foreigners displayed; for instance, being violent against the civilian population, confronting the police, et cetera. And I thought you said that at that meeting the proposal was made to decide, there and then, to send these people back. That was one option, and the other option was if you could not send them back, then at least be sure that they were incorporated properly into the army. And then you continued to say that General Delic accepted the proposal, and I was just not sure about which of the two proposals it was that he accepted. We know, as a result, from other testimonies, that in the end the foreigners stayed, so obviously they were not sent home. But I'm curious to know if actually it could have been decided at that morning meeting on the 18th of June to send back the foreigners. Was that a real option? And what was General Delic's position on it? What did he accept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Harhoff, your conclusion is correct, but, however, we did not say that it was supposed to be resolved in the field. We said that the army commander should discuss that issue with Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, and to make two proposals: The first one, to return those people where they had come from, and we at the staff did not know where they had come from. Option number 2 was given -- or provided that was impossible. And now we know much more about where those people had actually come from than we knew at the time. We proposed that they be incorporated into the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or, to be more specific, into the 3rd Corps. Therefore, I don't know what Commander Delic and the president of the Presidency finally decided. The events of the fortnight, well, I only recently saw that there was a document by which Commander Delic ordered that the El Mujahed Unit be formed. He was there with us, Commander Delic, and he was aware that we did not need those people for the simple reason that they did not fit inside the defence concept of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You are correct when you say that even today there are still those who should leave Bosnia-Herzegovina, 15 years later. I'm now referring to the 18th of June, 1993, when I learned of that for the first time. Perhaps others knew before me, but that was the first time that I heard specifically about this group of people that should have been made part of the regular army, with all its regulations and rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So the proposal to either send back the people or to integrate them was a proposal to be presented to the president of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And presumably General Delic then took these two proposals to President Izetbegovic. From the meeting, he brought forward the proposal to the president. And, in your view, was it then the president who ultimately decided to allow the foreigners to stay and to integrate them in the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm certain that Mr. Delic conveyed our opinions and the conclusions made at the staff. There were 13 of us; however, I cannot go about guessing as to who made the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this is probably the time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I have no further questions today, Your Honours, unless we're going to keep going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand it clearly. You have no further questions today?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. But I won't be very long tomorrow. I'll stay within the time frame that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are going to adjourn, and we'll come back tomorrow at 9.00 in the same court, sir. Okay. Sorry, I was still trying to warn the witness. Okay, did you hear that, sir? Tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.55 p.m.,
